scenarios.title: Depth and hydrostatic pressure: swim-bladder compression and the piezolyte depth ceiling

params.label: Depth below the surface
params.source: design input; 11,000 m is the deepest ocean

metrics.label: Absolute hydrostatic pressure
Swim-bladder gas volume relative to the surface (no secretion)
Whole-body density at depth (bladder sized for neutral buoyancy at the surface)
Net sinking force as a fraction of body weight
Muscle TMAO of marine teleosts at this depth (trend)
Internal osmolality of marine teleosts at this depth (trend)
Distance above the predicted teleost depth ceiling

equations: P(z) = P0 + rho_w g z
V_gas(z)/V_gas(0) = P0/P(z) (Boyle, isothermal, no secretion)
phi0 = 1 - rho_w/rho_t (bladder sized for neutral buoyancy at the surface), rho_t = 1.05 x 1025 kg/m3
rho_body(z) = rho_t (1 - phi0) / (1 - phi0 + phi0 P0/P(z)); sinking fraction = (rho_body - rho_w)/rho_body
TMAO(z) = 40 + 0.04557 z mmol/kg; osmolality(z) = 350 + 0.09157 z mOsm/kg
ceiling: osmolality(z) = 1100 mOsm/kg  =>  z = 8,190 m

sources.cite: Yancey PH, Gerringer ME, Drazen JC, Rowden AA, Jamieson A (2014). Marine fish may be biochemically constrained from inhabiting the deepest ocean depths. PNAS 111:4461-4465 (abstract)
Lauridsen H et al. (2022). Buoyancy and hydrostatic balance in a West Indian Ocean coelacanth Latimeria chalumnae. BMC Biol 20:180

Jamieson AJ, Swanborn DJB, Bond T et al. (2026). Faunal biodiversity of the lower abyssal and hadal zones of the Japan, Ryukyu and Izu-Ogasawara trenches (NW Pacific Ocean). Biodiversity Data Journal 14:e182172 (deepest recorded fish, 8,336 m)

modelCard.validity: Depth 0-7,000 m for the TMAO and osmolality trends (deeper is extrapolation, inRange false). The ceiling applies to marine teleosts. Boyle compression is exact physics for the gas but ignores gas secretion and the bladder wall.

params.source: design input

metrics.label: Still-air glide distance covered by the Lean bound, h (L/D)max
Level kinetic-energy phase, still air (OUTSIDE the Lean theorem)
Ground distance with wind, both phases (NOT covered by the Lean theorem)
Ground distance minus still-air distance (-u x time airborne)
Time airborne (bound)
Launch speed reachable by this organism
Minimum lift-supported airspeed
Speed over the water needed to reach v_min airspeed
Glide airspeed minus gust minus v_min (negative = stall in a lull)
Quasi-steady lift / weight in a gust peak

equations: launch speed v0 = organism's own (glide.mjs); cannot glide if v0 < v_min (all distances 0)
level phase: t_A = (L/D)_eff (v0 - v_min)/g; x_A,ground = (L/D)_eff (v0^2 - v_min^2)/(2g) - u t_A  (outside the Lean theorem)
descent from h at v_LD: t_B = h (L/D)/v_LD; x_B,ground = h (L/D) - u t_B  (the still-air part h (L/D) is the Lean-covered bound)
takeoff water speed = v_min - u
gust: stall margin = V - gust - v_min; load factor n = (1 + gust/V)^2
